options.text: Copy an angle at $R$ with no transversal that cuts line $k$, and claim the new line is parallel to $k$.
The finished parallel line is what creates the transversal through $k$.
Draw a transversal through $R$ that cuts $k$, copy the corresponding angle at $R$, and draw the new line through $R$.
Slide a set-square along $k$ and treat that tool method as this corresponding-angle copy.

stem:
Wafa has line $k$ and wants a line through point $R$ parallel to $k$ by copying a corresponding angle from a transversal.

Which plan works?

teacher.key_rationale: A transversal must cut k; copying the corresponding angle at R then drawing the new line through R makes it parallel to k. Omitting the transversal, reversing cause and effect, or swapping in a set-square slide all miss that construction.
